topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes for the hallmarks of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the framing for the lecture, introducing its learning outcomes and the conceptual framework of cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Growth signal autonomy and intracellular signaling pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in cell surface receptors and intracellular signaling cascades allow cancer cells to sustain proliferation independently of external growth cues.

topics.label: Block to terminal differentiation in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how oncogenic alterations arrest normal lineage differentiation while maintaining proliferative potential in hematologic and epithelial tissues.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptosis, senescence, and replicative immortality
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cancer cells circumvent cellular fail-safes including apoptosis, telomere shortening, and p53-mediated stress responses to achieve unlimited replicative potential.

topics.label: Metabolic rewiring and oncometabolites in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the metabolic alterations of cancer cells, detailing aerobic glycolysis and Krebs cycle mutations that produce oncometabolites to drive tumorigenesis.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how tumors activate the angiogenic switch to recruit vasculature required for oxygen and nutrient supply during progression.

topics.label: Mechanisms, dissemination, and genomics of tumor metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the multi-step cascade of cancer dissemination, including vascular invasion, clinical monitoring of circulating tumor cells, seed-and-soil interactions, and metastatic genomics.

topics.label: Summary and concluding remarks
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the lecture closing by synthesizing how cancer hallmarks integrate and directing students toward practical sessions.
